name: India–Pakistan
value: Treaty suspensions; airspace ban to 24 Nov
summary: Indus Waters Treaty stays suspended and Pakistan's airspace ban on Indian aircraft runs to 24 Nov; no strike found
state: Pakistan extended its ban on Indian aircraft using its airspace to 24 Nov, renewing a closure in place since the April 2025 Pahalgam attack (The Star, 20 Oct). India holds the Indus Waters Treaty in abeyance, and Pakistan has said any change to cross-border river flows would be treated as an act of war (Dawn, citing AFP). Searches on 14 Nov found no new Line of Control incident, cross-border strike or mobilisation. Ongoing treaty suspensions keep Watch.
for_you: Flights between India and Pakistan, and some routes across the region, remain disrupted by the airspace ban. Travellers can check FCDO travel advice for India and Pakistan, which covers areas near the Line of Control.
rubric_hit: Watch: treaty suspensions in force (Indus Waters Treaty; airspace ban to 24 Nov); no cross-border strike or mobilisation

sources.title: The Star — Pakistan extends ban on Indian aircraft using its airspace until Nov 24
Dawn — India 'actively working' to restrict water flows to Pakistan after Indus Waters Treaty suspension

why: Two nuclear-armed neighbours with a history of rapid escalation after terrorist attacks.
drivers: Kashmir attacks, Line of Control firing, water disputes (Indus), domestic politics.

rubric.watch: Ceasefire violations, a major terrorist attack with blame assigned, or treaty suspensions.
rubric.normal: Ceasefire holding along the Line of Control; no major attacks.
